nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf06195-job. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Read Pending Queue (Notion)
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Keep Valid Jobs
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Work in Batches
nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 5 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.name: Process Batch Item
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/jobs — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Respect Rate Limits
nodes.notes: Pauses 2 seconds — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Aggregate Batch Results
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Mark Completed in Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Job Tracker', matched on jobId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Job Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Job Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per job (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Pipe API callbacks with Google Sheets and Slack

**Pattern:** Webhook Pipeline · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers utilities work end to end across Google Sheets, Slack and Notion.

It moves through 26 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Read Pending Queue (Notion)
3. Keep Valid Jobs
4. Work in Batches
5. Process Batch Item
6. Respect Rate Limits
7. Aggregate Batch Results
8. Mark Completed in Google Sheets
9. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
10. Archive Row Snapshot
11. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
12. Record Sub-workflow Result
13. Load Previous Snapshot
14. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Enrich with Reference Data
18. Fold In Enrichment Fields
19. Stamp Completion Time
20. Persist Run Metadata
21. Save Execution Metadata
22. Sort Jobs Newest First
23. Align Field Names
24. Summarize Run Stats
25. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
26. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing utilities work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Pending Queue (Notion) → Keep Valid Jobs → Work in Batches → Process Batch Item → Respect Rate Limits → Aggregate Batch Results → Mark Completed in Google Sheets → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Sort Jobs Newest First → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for utilities
- Utilities sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Google Sheets
- A backlog too large to push into Google Sheets in one pass, across 29 nodes
- Pushing utilities events into Google Sheets and Slack the moment they land, not on the next poll

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for utilities, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Slack are skipped, across all 29 nodes of this utilities build
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 29 nodes in this utilities build
- The pause before Google Sheets is durable — a utilities run survives a restart
- Batches the work so Google Sheets rate limits never break a utilities run

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The batch size and the Wait between iterations exist specifically to respect the downstream API's rate limit — processing everything as fast as possible just gets the workflow throttled or banned. Marking items completed only after a batch succeeds leaves a clean resume point if the run dies mid-way, instead of an ambiguous half-processed state.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Lower the batch size and raise the wait — measure the throughput/reliability tradeoff directly.
2. Simulate a failed item mid-batch and see exactly what 'Mark Completed' captures.
3. Point the queue read at a different store platform.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole utilities payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your utilities process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
